newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's future government may soften right curbs - aide.
newsitem.headline: HK's future government may soften right curbs - aide.

text.p: A key member of Hong Kong's future government signalled on Wednesday that it might soften controversial proposals to curb civil liberties.

Henry Tang, a member of the Executive Council of future leader Tung Chee-hwa, indicated the government-in-waiting was likely to respond positively to demands for a more liberal approach reflected in a three-week pulsetaking of public views.
"There are many proposals that have been put forward to us," Tang told reporters.
"In the consultation exercise, there are more liberal (proposals) than what is in the consultation document," Tang, who also heads the territory's federation of industry, said.
"I'm saying that yes, I think, some of them are worthy of our consideration and they will be considered and finalised."
A month ago Tung launched a plan to tighten control on civil and political liberties in the British-ruled territory after it reverts to Beijing's control at midnight on June 30.

His proposal included introducing police permits for political protests and a ban on foreign funding of local political groups. Pro-democracy movements and lawyers in Hong Kong have strongly protested against these moves.

Tang hinted that the proposal requiring police approval for demonstrations one week in advance might be softened and the ban on foreign donations to local political parties might have to be reconsidered.
